passage: I'm Chaitanya, Pradeep's desk partner. On Monday he was very quiet. At lunch he kept turning his spoon over and said both his parents say awful things about each other to him, and each one wants him to carry messages. "I love both," he said. I did not know what to say, so I just sat there. He looked at his hands. Later I saw him in the corridor telling the class teacher, "I don't want to stand between them." His voice was steady when he said it, but I can't tell how he really felt. I only know he looked a little lighter afterwards.

qa.q: Who did Pradeep tell that he did not want to stand between them?
qa.a: He told the class teacher in the corridor.

qa.q: How can you tell Pradeep felt torn between his parents?
qa.a: He kept turning his spoon over, said both parents say awful things about each other, and said he loves both.

qa.q: What could Pradeep say to each parent to protect himself?
qa.a: He can tell them kindly that he loves both of them and does not want to carry messages or stand between them.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya have felt listening to Pradeep at lunch?
qa.a: Chaitanya did not know what to say, so Chaitanya probably felt unsure, wanted to help without knowing how, and stayed beside Pradeep instead.

grounding: A classmate observes a child who loves both parents and says he does not want to be in the middle.

passage:
In their flat in Malmö, Noa's mum said, "Your father never cared about anything but work. Tell him I need the money for your shoes."
At her dad's place on the weekend, he said, "Your mum is so controlling. Ask her why she won't let me come to your concert."
Noa felt stretched like an elastic band. She loved them both.
On Sunday, when Dad asked again, she put down her fork. "Keep me out of the middle. I'm not carrying messages."
Dad was quiet for a moment. "You're right. That's not fair on you."
Monday, she said the same to her mum, Ulla. Ulla nodded slowly.

qa.q: How did Noa feel when both parents asked her to carry messages?
qa.a: She felt torn and stretched like an elastic band, because she loved them both.

qa.q: What wise thing did Noa say?
qa.a: She asked to be kept out of the middle and said she would not carry messages.

qa.q: How might Noa's dad see what he'd been doing?
qa.a: After Noa spoke, her dad seemed to realise it wasn't fair to put her in the middle.

grounding: Each parent badmouths the other and asks a girl to pass messages; she feels torn and says she does not want to be in the middle.

passage:
In the school counsellor's room, Santosh stared at the carpet. "Papa says Mummy lies about everything. Mummy says Papa doesn't care. And they both ask me what the other one said."
Rajni Ma'am listened. "How does that feel?"
"Like I'm a spy. I hate it. I love them both."
"You're allowed to ask them to keep you out of the middle," she said. "Want to practise?"
Santosh tried. "Please keep me out of the middle." His voice was small. He tried again, louder.
Rajni Ma'am said she'd also call both parents that week. That evening Santosh told Papa. Papa looked surprised, then nodded.

qa.q: Where did Santosh talk to Rajni Ma'am?
How did Santosh feel about being asked what each parent said?
qa.a: He felt like a spy and hated it, torn because he loved them both.

qa.q: How did Rajni Ma'am help Santosh?
qa.a: She listened, told him he could ask to be kept out of the middle, helped him practise, and planned to call both parents.

qa.q: How might Papa have felt when Santosh spoke up?
qa.a: Papa seemed surprised at first, then accepted what Santosh said.

grounding: A boy whose parents each badmouth the other feels like a spy; with a counsellor's help he practises saying he does not want to be in the middle.
